principle: Every technique must prove, explain, orient, compare, evoke, or deliberately delight without competing with the argument.

techniques.name: Stable semantic crop
techniques.purpose: Keep the meaningful subject, eyes, hands, and lead room framed without nervous tracking.
techniques.fallback: Use a stable centre crop for the entire source shot.

techniques.name: Semantic punch-in
techniques.purpose: Increase intimacy or emphasis only when a spoken beat earns it.

techniques.name: Speaker and reaction bridge
techniques.purpose: Preserve conversational meaning through motivated speaker, listener, J-cut, and L-cut choices.
techniques.fallback: Use the stable mixed programme view.

techniques.name: Living evidence theatre
techniques.purpose: Bring an approved source into the physical visual world while retaining its credibility and attribution.
techniques.fallback: Use a static, attributed evidence card in clear negative space.

techniques.name: Gesture-directed composition
techniques.purpose: Place the approved visual where Krish naturally points or looks so performance and proof act as one shot.
techniques.fallback: Use detected negative space without implying a gesture connection.

techniques.name: Guided evidence pan and magnifier
techniques.purpose: Direct the eye through a dense screenshot or document in the order needed to understand the claim.
techniques.fallback: Use a static crop of the one decisive region.

techniques.name: Owned sketch reveal
techniques.purpose: Animate Krish's exact drawing as a thinking instrument without inventing marks.
techniques.fallback: Reveal the untouched sketch as a static insert.

techniques.name: Vertical evidence descent
techniques.purpose: Let a sequence of real artefacts descend through the frame as a causal chain rather than a collage.
techniques.fallback: Use one artefact at a time with clean cuts.

techniques.name: Evidence to illustration handoff
techniques.purpose: Show authentic proof first, then clearly transition into a labelled interpretation of its implication.
techniques.fallback: Keep the evidence on screen and explain the implication through captions only.

techniques.name: Full-frame inspection
techniques.purpose: Temporarily give the entire portrait frame to evidence or an artefact when comprehension is the primary task.
techniques.fallback: Use a sidecar while the speaker remains visible.

techniques.name: Depth-layered reality
techniques.purpose: Separate foreground, subject, and proof planes to create spatial storytelling while preserving factual roles.

techniques.name: Evidence portal
techniques.purpose: Move through a real approved artefact into the next scene as a motivated transition.
techniques.fallback: Use a match cut on the focal region.

techniques.name: Camera motion relay
techniques.purpose: Carry one motivated movement across real and generated or illustrated planes as a single visual sentence.

techniques.name: Stylised presenter duplicate
techniques.purpose: Create a clearly illustrative duplicate of Krish for comparison, conflict, or counterfactual structure.
techniques.fallback: Use a labelled split-screen freeze frame.

techniques.name: Reality rupture
techniques.purpose: Use one surprising, obviously authored visual break to embody a conceptual turn.
techniques.fallback: Use a smash cut and sound bridge.
